summary: 从众既可能源于想融入群体，也可能源于对自己判断的不确定。文章从校园风潮写到阿希的线段实验，再用不同形式的从众解释个体和情境差异。
logic: 设计线段比较与错误多数
观察个人怎样回应压力
解释从众形式和信心差异

paragraphs.brief: 当你实际上站在一边，思考我们多么容易地被说服，拥有某些物品是我们确保心灵平静的唯一方法，你可以看到什么是重要的概念一致性。
sentences: During your childhood, there will have been some kind of craze which affected all the people in your school.
在你的童年，会有某种疯狂影响所有的人在你的学校。
It may have been to do with a particular toy or possibly a must-have item of clothing.
这可能与某个玩具有关，也可能与一定的衣物有关。
It may have been something as simple as a type of pen or as expensive as an electronic games console.
这可能是像笔一样简单的东西或者是像电子游戏控制台一样昂贵的东西
Fashion designers, toy manufacturers and anyone else involved in the retail trade love conformity.
时装设计师玩具制造商以及任何参与零售行业的人都喜欢上他
Set up a craze, especially in the young, and everyone will go for it.
设置一个疯狂，特别是年轻人，每个人都会去。
In fact, it’s an ideal way to sell huge quantities of merchandise.
事实上，这是销售大量商品的理想方式。
The levels of conformity in consumerism are phenomenal.
消费主义的一致程度是惊人的。
When you actually stand back and consider how easily we are persuaded that having certain items is the only way we can ensure peace of mind, you see what an important concept conformity is.
当你实际上站在一边，思考我们多么容易地被说服，拥有某些物品是我们确保心灵平静的唯一方法，你可以看到什么是重要的概念一致性。

paragraphs.brief: 遵守被描述为“对群体压力的屈服”(Crutchfield，1962年)。
sentences: Conformity has been described as “yielding to group pressure” (Crutchfield, 1962).
遵守被描述为“对群体压力的屈服”(Crutchfield，1962年)。
However, this implies that other people put pressure on us to make us conform and this is not always the case.
然而，这意味着其他人对我们施加压力，要求我们遵守，但情况并非总是如此。
A better definition is given by Aronson (1976) who said it was a “change in a person’s behaviour or opinions as a result of real or imagined pressure from a person or group of people”.
Aronson(1976年)给出了更好的定义，他说，这是 " 一个人的行为或意见因个人或群体的实际或想象的压力而发生变化 "。
This would make more sense, as often the pressure we feel is imagined.
这样做更有意义，因为我们经常感觉到我们想象的压力。
The person or group he refers to would have to be important to us at the time, regardless of their status.
他提到的个人或团体，无论他们的地位如何，当时都必须对我们很重要。

paragraphs.brief: 第一批研究之一考察了人们在要求估计瓶中豆子数量时给出的答案(Jenness，1932)。
sentences: There has been considerable research on conformity.
已经对符合性进行了大量研究。
One of the first studies looked at the answers people gave when asked to estimate the number of beans in a bottle (Jenness, 1932).
第一批研究之一考察了人们在要求估计瓶中豆子数量时给出的答案(Jenness，1932)。
If you have ever entered a “guess the number” competition, you probably looked at the previous estimates made and based your judgment on what other people had guessed.
如果你曾经参加过“猜测数字”的竞赛，你也许可以看一下先前所作的估计，并根据其他人的猜测作出判断。
This is more or less what happened in the Jenness study.
简尼斯研究中发生的情况差不多是这样
First of all, he asked the respondents to give their own estimates, and then he asked them to decide a group estimate.
首先，他要求被调查者提供自己的估计数，然后他要求他们决定一个小组估计数。
Finally, he asked them alone again and discovered that they had stayed with the group answer.
最后，他再次单独问他们，发现他们一直听小组的答复。

paragraphs.brief: 也许是阿施(1951年)进行的关于遵守问题最著名的研究，当时他制造了这样一种局面，即他的许多臣民给出的答案是公然不真实的，而不是与他们同在的人相矛盾。
sentences: Probably the most famous study on conformity was undertaken by Asch (1951) when he created a situation where many of his subjects gave answers which were blatantly untrue, rather than contradict the people they were with.
也许是阿施(1951年)进行的关于遵守问题最著名的研究，当时他制造了这样一种局面，即他的许多臣民给出的答案是公然不真实的，而不是与他们同在的人相矛盾。
He did this by getting his subject to sit round a table with six stooges (colleagues of the experimenter) so that the subject was second to last.
他让实验对象和6个木偶(实验者的同事)一起坐在一个圆桌会议上，使实验对象位居第二。

He showed them all a large card which had three lines of different lengths drawn on it, labelled A, B and C. He then gave them a card with a single line and asked them to match this in terms of length to one of the lines A, B or C.
他向他们展示了一张大卡片，上面有三行不同的长度，标有A、B和C的标签。然后他给了他们一张单行的卡片，并要求他们用长度来与A、B或C的长度匹配。

paragraphs.brief: Asch在审判后采访了他的当事人，试图了解他们为什么遵从一个显然错误的答案。
sentences: The stooges gave untrue responses in a number of the trials and the subjects were left in the situation where they either reported what they saw with their own eyes or conformed to the norm of the group.
傀儡们在一些审判中作出了不实的答复，他们要么自己目光报道自己所看到的，要么遵守小组的规范。
When the results were assessed, Asch found that in one out of every three trials where the wrong answer was given, the subject gave the same wrong answer as the stooges.
在评估结果时，Asch发现，每三次审判中，有一次作出错误的回答，而当事人给出的答案与小卒相同。
This led to an average level of conformity of 32 per cent.
这导致平均达标率为32%。
Asch interviewed his subjects after the trials to try to find out why they conformed to an answer which was so obviously wrong.
Asch在审判后采访了他的当事人，试图了解他们为什么遵从一个显然错误的答案。
Most of them said that they did not want to cause problems within the group, although they also stated that when they did give wrong answers it made them anxious.
多数人说，他们不想在群体内造成问题，但他们也说，当他们作出错误的回答时，他们很焦虑。

(Asch found that when there was just one other person present who did not go along with the majority, no matter how many others there were, it was sufficient to make the subject give the right answer.)
(Asch认为，如果只有一人在场，而他没有同意多数意见，无论有多少其他人，只要让问题得到正确的答案就足够了。)

paragraphs.brief: 首先是遵守，让主体与人群一起防止任何群体内的敌意或不良感觉，并保持群体和谐。
sentences: Kelman (1953) outlined three processes which can explain social conformity.
Kelman(1953年)概述了可以解释社会一致性的三个过程。
The first is compliance, where subjects go along with the crowd to prevent any in-group hostility or bad feeling and to maintain group harmony.
首先是遵守，让主体与人群一起防止任何群体内的敌意或不良感觉，并保持群体和谐。
However, they do not change their own private belief.
然而，他们并没有改变自己的私人信仰。
If we look back to the Asch study, we can see that the subjects were simply complying with the demands of the experimental situation but hadn’t actually internalized the group’s norms.
如果我们回头看Asch的研究，我们可以看到，对象只是符合实验情况的要求，但实际上并没有内部化的小组的规范。
They agreed in public, but dissented in private.
他们公开同意，但私下表示异议。
In a process known as internalization, however, subjects do actually see the view of the group as the more valid one.
然而，在一个被称为内部化的过程中，主体确实认为集团的观点比较有效。
They may be able to do this, for example, by convincing themselves that their eyesight is poor.
例如，他们可以说服自己，他们的视力很差，从而做到这一点。
Sometimes, however, subjects actually seem to change their beliefs because they want to become more like their heroes.
然而，有时，主体似乎实际上改变了他们的信仰，因为他们想变得更像他们的英雄。
If they really want to become part of an in-group, they will start to identify with that group and take on the group’s values and beliefs, even if they are different to their own.
如果他们真的想成为集团的一部分，他们就会开始认同该集团，接受该集团的价值观和信仰，即使它们与自己不同。
Kelman calls this identification.
凯尔曼叫这个身份证明
It frequently happens with teenagers who want to become more like a peer group in order to be accepted, and suddenly seem to go against all the values and beliefs of their parents.
青少年为了被接受往往想成为同龄群体突然之间似乎与父母的所有价值观和信仰背道而驰

paragraphs.brief: 但是，对我们大多数人来说，我们每天感到多有信心，这取决于我们所处的局势，这可能影响行为。
sentences: So why is it that we have to conform?
那么为什么我们必须遵守？
Some people feel confident most of the time, have high self-esteem and do not have to go along with the majority.
有些人大部分时间都感到自信，自尊心高涨，不必接受大多数人的意见。
For most of us, though, how confident we feel varies from day to day, depending on the situation we are in, and this can influence behaviour.
但是，对我们大多数人来说，我们每天感到多有信心，这取决于我们所处的局势，这可能影响行为。

items.en: Childhood crazes can centre on items of any value.
items.zh: 童年的疯狂可以集中在任何有价值的东西上。
items.why: 作者用一支普通的笔和昂贵的游戏机作对照，说明童年热潮既可能围绕廉价物品，也可能围绕高价物品。

items.en: Children are more vulnerable to crazes now than they used to be.
items.zh: 儿童现在比过去更容易受到疯狂的伤害。
items.why: 文中说追赶热潮的现象在年轻人中尤其常见，却没有将今天的儿童与过去的儿童作时间上的比较。

items.en: Consumers make too many quick decisions in shops.
items.zh: 消费者在商店里做出太多的快速决定。
items.why: 作者讲的是消费者容易受从众心理影响、相信某些东西非买不可。文中没有评价购物决策有多快，或这样的快速决定是否过多。

items.en: Crutchfield’s definition of conformity is the most reliable.
items.zh: Crutchfield对符合性的定义是最可靠的。
items.why: 作者先引述克拉奇菲尔德的定义，随后明确说阿伦森的定义“更好”，因为群体压力有时只是个人想象出来的。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: Studies on conformity In the Jenness study, people had to guess how many ________ were in a container.
items.zh: 在詹尼斯的从众研究中，受试者要猜容器里有多少 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“第一批研究之一考察了人们在要求估计瓶中豆子数量时给出的答案(Jenness，1932)”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Jenness found that, in most cases, people opted for an estimate given by a ________.
items.zh: 詹尼斯发现，多数情况下，人们会采用一个 ________ 给出的估计数。
items.why: 回到对应内容“首先，他要求被调查者提供自己的估计数，然后他要求他们决定一个小组估计数”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Asch asked his subjects to ________ line lengths.
items.zh: 阿希要求受试者按长度 ________ 线段。
items.why: 回到对应内容“他向他们展示了一张大卡片，上面有三行不同的长度，标有A、B和C的标签。然后他给了他们一张单行的卡片，并要求他们用长度来与A、B或C的长度匹配”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: To test the extent to which people would conform, he placed his subjects with colleagues who gave ________ responses.
items.zh: 为了测试受试者会在多大程度上从众，他让他们与故意给出 ________ 回答的研究同事一起答题。
items.why: 同义可为 wronglincorrect,但原文用 untrue,优先原词。

items.en: He found that his subjects agreed with his colleagues 32% of the time, although they admitted to feeling ________ about giving their answer.
items.zh: 阿希发现，受试者有32%的时候会同意这些同事的答案，但他们承认，在作答时感到 ________。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: In Kelman’s account, compliance is illustrated by the research conducted by ________.
items.zh: 在凯尔曼的解释中，可以用 ________ 的研究来说明“顺从”。
items.why: 回到对应内容“如果我们回头看Asch的研究，我们可以看到，对象只是符合实验情况的要求，但实际上并没有内部化的小组的规范”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In the process known as ________, people persuade themselves that the majority view is best despite their own ideas.
items.zh: 在称为 ________ 的过程中，尽管自己另有看法，人们还是说服自己相信多数人的观点最好。

items.en: In the second process, the majority view is considered the most ________ view.
items.zh: 在第二种过程中，人们认为多数人的看法最 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“然而，在一个被称为内部化的过程中，主体确实认为集团的观点比较有效”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In the process called ________, people change their ideas to those of the majority.
items.zh: 在称为 ________ 的过程中，人们改变自己的想法，使之与多数人一致。
items.why: 回到对应内容“凯尔曼叫这个身份证明”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The process in which people change their ideas to those of the majority is typical of ________.
items.zh: 改变自己的想法以符合多数人的看法，这种过程在 ________ 身上很典型。

clauses: During your childhood, there will have been some kind of craze ….
“which affected all the people in your school”修饰前面的 kind。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 kind，再把修饰信息接回主句。
“that other people put pressure on us to make us conform and this is not always the case”补足 implies 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 implies 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
